yes: The post, reading any emoji as the words, groups or actions they stand for, directs abuse or contempt at a group identity (such as race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender, sexuality, disability, immigration status or class) or at someone because of that identity, explicitly or implicitly: insults and slurs, threats, dehumanising comparisons, or subtle digs and hostile stereotypes.
no: The post, reading any emoji for what they stand for, does not attack a group identity: it may mention identities, swear, criticise, counter hate or target something that is not an identity (an animal, an object, a person for non-identity reasons), but it is not abusive towards an identity group or anyone because of their identity.
not hateful: The post, reading any emoji for what they stand for, contains no abuse towards a group identity or its members, even if it mentions identities, swears, criticises, pushes back against hate or is aggressive towards something that is not an identity.
derogation: The post explicitly insults, demeans or demonises an identity group: slurs, portraying the group as bad, inferior, criminal or a threat, saying it is unwelcome, or openly stating hatred or disgust for it, without likening it to non-humans (dehumanization) or calling for action against it (threatening language).
animosity: The post is negative towards an identity group only implicitly or subtly: jokes or mockery playing on stereotypes, claims the group gets undeserved special treatment, dog whistles or prejudiced pseudo-facts; if the insult is stated outright it is derogation instead.
dehumanization: The post maliciously describes, compares or equates an identity group or its members with non-humans such as vermin, apes, pigs, snakes, insects, disease, trash, robots, aliens, monsters or demons, including by standing an animal or object emoji in for the group or by word play on the group's name; a comparison that does not demean the group is not enough.
threatening language: The post states, wishes for, supports, urges or celebrates taking action that inflicts harm on an identity group or its members, such as violence, killing, attacks or kicking them out; merely saying a group is unwelcome, without calling for action, is derogation.
